title: Orca module organization execution tracker
sequenceAuthority: This tracker supersedes the original audit phase ordering. Audit proposals remain the baseline ownership inventory.

activitySample.interpretation: Development edit traffic proxy, not production usage. Bounded first-parent checkout history; includes merged change names, ignores unmerged work, rename following and other branches. Not a full calendar-week or lifetime assessment. Refresh before each code PR.

cadence: Work over multiple days in merge-sized PRs. First milestone is the quiet-area wave; no fixed completion date. Later discovery can add PRs; ordering adapts to live work and review capacity.

rules.noBarrels: No new export * or export { ... } from another local module as a convenience API; no index.ts aggregation, folder imports relying on index resolution, or old-path forwarding modules. Import the concrete owner file directly. Existing re-export chains inside moved code must be reviewed and flattened for affected consumers when they only forward ownership; keep any contractually required external package export surface explicit and documented.
rules.scope: One responsibility per PR; move code and relevant tests, update all callers atomically, and preserve behavior. Keep unrelated redesign, broad symbol renames, formatting and dependency upgrades out.
rules.naming: Final responsibility folders and descriptive basenames must be settled before opening a PR. No generic helpers/utils/common folders. Do not schedule a second whole-repo rename just to shorten prefixes. Larger path suggestions need boundary review before use.
rules.atomicCallers: A batch moves its modules and updates every current caller, mocks and path-string reference in the same PR. No temporary compatibility re-export stubs, even when splitting a scope across PRs.
rules.size: Aim for 5-20 production modules per move PR. More than 25 production modules, 60 moved files or 100 caller/path-reference edits triggers a split review before implementation. These are review prompts, not permission to divide an ownership unit arbitrarily.
rules.sequence: Default is one code-move PR open at a time. Merge required green checks, then start the next PR from updated main. Sequence dependencies are workflow ordering, not claims of code dependencies. No long stack or multiple days of stale parallel moves.
rules.revalidate: Before each PR, refresh the bounded activity sample and exact file/caller inventory at current main. If this group or required callers are actively changing, choose the next quieter eligible group and record why. Never infer absence of active PRs from Git history.
rules.tests: All test/app invocations use ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1. Run the relevant existing tests and required CI checks. Add tests only if a meaningful gap or bug is uncovered; keep fixes separate from the move when possible.
rules.merge: Do not mark done on branch creation, PR open or green local tests. Require merged PR URL, merge SHA, check evidence and updated inventory. Revert the atomic PR if it causes a regression; do not restore aliases or forwarding exports.
rules.review: Apply .agents/skills/refactor-audit/SKILL.md before each code PR merge: compare against the merge base, audit moved bodies, literals, callers and wire names, obtain an independent sub-agent review, port upstream fixes into their new owners on rebase, and run the skill's merge-validation gate. Record findings and resolutions.

commonCompletionCriteria: Named concrete responsibility and file destinations reviewed; no barrels or source-path forwarding modules.
Production modules and relevant tests moved; every direct caller, mock and runtime/build/script reference updated atomically.
Existing targeted tests, affected typechecks, changed-code quality, formatting and required PR CI checks pass with commands recorded.
Review export/import changes for cycles, lazy-loading changes and behavior; preserve wire, storage, channel and process output names.
Complete the refactor-audit skill and independent sub-agent review; record findings, resolutions and merge-validation evidence.
Record merged PR URL, merge SHA, actual moved paths, affected consumers, check evidence and map update.
Rebase the next task on merged main; resolve conflicts by rechecking actual ownership, never restoring forwarding aliases.
commandNotation: Commands containing angle brackets are templates filled from current changed files before execution; conditional commands apply only when their stated condition holds. Set ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1 for tests/apps. Run applicable repository CI, including import-boundary and ratchet gates, rather than adding baseline exemptions.

desktop.review: Run existing affected tests at their new paths; include outside callers and source-reading tests. Check Electron/plain-Node separation.

commands: pnpm tc:node when moved paths are explicitly included by node tsconfig
renderer.review: Preserve lazy module boundaries, React identities, store subscriptions and draft ownership. If rendered UI validation is needed, use the electron skill and hidden Playwright CDP.

shared.review: Select suites from actual consumers; preserve wire and stored formats, old/new client compatibility and generated RPC ownership. Include cloud checks only if its consumers are affected.

mobile.review: Keep native/web variants together; inspect Metro, generated WebView references, direct shared imports and touch/keyboard behavior.

tooling.review: Check package scripts, CI workflows, source-reading tests, import.meta paths and copied fixtures; preserve generated artifacts.

cloud.review: Use the independent cloud workspace; preserve director/cell assignment and rolling-version contracts. This task does not deploy anything.

commands: pnpm run build:electron-vite when built entry sources change
process.review: Check build-entry and launch-path references, stable output filenames, Windows/WSL and macOS/Linux. Use existing isolated platform/CI checks; run app tests with background launch.

statusNotes: Only verified tasks are complete. Record blockers in blockers while retaining lifecycle status. Discovery keep decisions use the directory decision fields and evidence. Planning itself is complete; every implementation/merge task is still planned.

forwarderAudit.method: TypeScript AST inspection of all selected production-classified modules; relative export-from declarations and named exports of imported local bindings recorded. Pure forwarding means every top-level statement is import/export/empty. This is source forwarding analysis, not full typechecker provenance. Required external package exports are a separate boundary review.

scopes.scopeNote: Seven adjacent transport files already form a named provider family. Keep them separate from the backend client.
Jira registration, request validation, cancellation and metadata handling belong together within IPC.
Attachment discovery, authenticated image fetching, grants, caching and protocols are a concrete subdomain.
The issue-context family covers resolution, optional includes, pagination and relations around one public read operation.
Repository settings have one user-facing owner and a large mixed family of components, state and tests.
VM provisioning, recipe execution, resume and SSH cleanup currently occupy the application root.
Cookie reading, importing and cleanup are a concrete subsystem inside a 611-file directory.
Group one product-specific tool family; build-, run- and check- prefixes describe verbs, not ownership.
Relay assignment is a named operational responsibility in an otherwise flat service root.
Finish the existing feature folder instead of creating another feature root. Most provider routing needs a later review inside its existing provider folders.
Consolidate the flat filesystem and watcher families with the existing filesystem folder, then consider a watcher child.
Status reduction, subscriptions and tests are scattered beside unrelated Zustand slices.
A concrete session-rule family can leave the 1,292-file renderer lib root without inventing a generic helpers directory.
The app-server protocol family is a more useful boundary than the broad codex filename prefix.
Structured Claude session execution is a distinct provider mode within an already named provider folder.
Give pure Jira contracts and rules a domain home, matching the existing shared Linear domain.
Remote runtime handshake, capabilities and transport contracts are one discoverable protocol domain.
Chat data and pure rules need a concrete domain home rather than hundreds of sibling names.
Agent-session contracts are a large cross-surface domain currently encoded in filenames.
The phone's chat family is mixed into a 722-file session folder, including presentation, interaction and hooks.
Session lifecycle and persistence should be discoverable below the runtime composition layer.
Consolidate flat terminal transport files into the existing pty tree after agreeing its ownership boundaries.
The existing persistence subtree and flat root tests split the same discovery trail.
